 There’s good news for the 90% of taxpayers that claim this popular deduction
 Leada Gore Tue, November 10, 2026 at 10:54 AM PST 2 min read There are several options when it comes to deductions when filing taxes. Some people choose to itemize their deductions. The vast majority, however, – 90% of taxpayers – don't list deductions but instead file what's known as a standard deduction. 
 Standard deductions are a fixed dollar amount that reduces taxable income and therefore the money people owe. In many cases, the standard deduction is larger than itemized amounts and because claiming it is easier than identifying and totaling expenses. 
 Just as tax brackets adjust each year to account for inflation, the standard deduction is also changing in 2027. 
 Here are the new figures for 2027: 
 Married filing jointly and surviving spouses - $33,200, up $1,000 
 Heads of households - $24,925, up $775 
 Single - $16,600, up $500 
 Married filing separately - $16,600, up $500 
 There are additional standard deductions for taxpayers over age 65. In 2027, filers over age 65 or those with blindness can claim extra deductions of: 
 $2,100 for single or head of household 
 $1,700 per person for married filing jointly or separately (per qualifying spouse) 
 There are special deductions in place through 2028 as well. 
 There is an additional $6,000 per eligible individual - $12,000 per married couple if both qualify – available through 2028 tax year. This bonus begins to phase out if Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) exceeds $75,000 for single filers or $150,000 for married couples filing jointly.
